# Why Ours-S loses to B9+ under COMMIT on d1_open (mechanism, exploratory)

**Status: EXPLORATORY, POST HOC (not pre-registered); associations within the frozen test run, not causal effects.** Generated by `python -m analysis.v2_mechanism_d1` (`docs/research_v2/mechanism_v2.json`). The frozen evaluator (`simulator/e3v2_lazy.frozen_records`) was re-run offline for Ours-v2[COMMIT] (Ours-S) and B9+ on the frozen bundles; outcomes come from the existing Phase A test store; nothing was generated or graded and no judge was called.

**Gate passed:** the recomputed per-item Δ[COMMIT] equals `contrasts_test.json` for every cell and item (d1_open: 24 cells, 89,616 item-cells, max |diff| 0.0e+00); the three-part decomposition sums to the frozen per-item Δ to ≤ 1e-12. Bootstrap: paired item bootstrap of `analysis/v2_test_d1.py` (B = 10,000, seed 20261017); the primary Δ_C CI reproduces the frozen result (True).

## Summary

In the primary d1_open cell, Ours-S's deficit against B9+ (Δ_C -0.0367 [-0.0481, -0.0252]) is an accuracy deficit: the accuracy part is -0.0502 [-0.0617, -0.0385], partly offset by a latency gain of +0.0182 [+0.0161, +0.0203] (its answers start 105 ms sooner on average) and a compute cost of -0.0047 [-0.0052, -0.0043] (it retrieves on 99.1% of items vs 89.6%).
Practically all of the deficit sits on the 2,382 items (64%) where both controllers retrieve but Ours-S dispatches at an earlier partial (contribution -0.0374 [-0.0477, -0.0269]); where both dispatch at the same step (965 items) the outcomes are identical, and the items on which only Ours-S retrieves contribute +0.0007 [-0.0041, +0.0056].
On those items Ours-S's query had heard on average 77% of the question against 89% for B9+'s, found a gold passage in the top 3 less often (hit@3 -0.164 [-0.182, -0.146]) and answered correctly less often (accuracy -0.105), which outweighed its latency gain there (+0.047 utility per item).
Ours-S also dispatched more often on partials that the ASR later revised (54.5% vs 35.9% of retrievals; 20.6% vs 16.4% ignoring the last word), and the deficit is concentrated on those items (mean Δ_i -0.077 vs +0.011 on unrevised early partials, difference -0.088 [-0.111, -0.066]); but revision goes together with dispatching early: ignoring the last word the difference shrinks to -0.035 [-0.067, -0.004], and within bins of the fraction of the question heard it excludes zero in only 1 of 4 bins (0 of 4 ignoring the last word), so these data do not separate a revised query from a merely incomplete one.
The frozen objective anticipated only part of this cost: on the earlier-dispatch items its own quality term (each controller's belief and dev-measured ρ at dispatch, mean ρ 0.55 vs 0.33) implied an accuracy difference of -0.058 [-0.060, -0.057], against a realised -0.105 [-0.121, -0.089] (difference -0.047 [-0.063, -0.030]).
On text150, whose prefixes are never revised, the two controllers dispatch at the same step on 97.8% of the items where both retrieve and Δ_C is -0.0024 [-0.0072, +0.0022] (Ours-S's extra retrievals buy accuracy +0.0161, offset by latency -0.0143 and compute -0.0042); all of this is a post hoc description of one frozen test run, and it does not show that early dispatch or revision causes the loss.

## What these data do not show

* The analysis is post hoc and exploratory; its strata are defined by the controllers' own decisions, so differences between strata are associations, not effects of revision or timing.
* Accuracy differences on items where both controllers retrieve come from different passages (different dispatch points), but the answer cells were generated once per passage list and seed; no counterfactual answer was generated for this analysis.
* The final-transcript answer cell exists only where some controller in the frozen plan landed on it (lazy evaluation); here it existed for every early retrieval analysed (counts in the table), but it was generated because of the frozen plan, not for this analysis.
* Items whose partials get revised may be harder for ASR and retrieval in general (B9+ is also less accurate on them), so accuracy by revision status mixes partial quality with item difficulty; the paired Δ_i is the cleaner comparison.
* The model-vs-realised comparison uses each controller's own belief at a different step and the frozen quality term (ρ scales g₊ only); a gap can come from the dev ρ table, the belief calibration or that functional form, and these data do not tell which.
* d2_support results are judge-graded (Deviation D3: judge-validation gate not passed) and exploratory; partial-quality analyses (section 3) were run on d1_open only.
